text.p: Thousands of Israelis held simultaneous peace demonstrations in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv on Saturday evening.
In Tel Aviv about 2,000 people gathered at Yitzhak Rabin square, renamed after the prime minister assassinated last year by a right-wing Jew for his peace moves with the Arabs.
The protesters held torches and stood in the formation of the word "Shalom," the Hebrew word for peace.
In Jerusalem hundreds of left-wing Israelis, holding torches and waving pro-peace placards, marched to the official residence of Prime Minister Benjamin Netnayahu.

The demonstrators began their march from a square in the heart of Jerusalem where they were addressed by well known peace activists who praised last Wednesday's landmark meeting between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"Settlements are an obstacle to peace," and "peace now" read some of the signs. Netanyahu told a party convention on Thursday that he would continue to settle occupied land in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Protesters at both demonstrations called on the government to continue in the path of peace by fulfilling its commitments to the Palestinians including a long delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron.
Some 400 Jews live among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron, a flashpoint of violence.

Under an agreement signed between the PLO and the previous Israeli government, Israel was to have redeployed its troops in March but delayed the move for security reasons. Netanyahu has said he is studying the situation.
